email.subject1: a signal play for Placer civic
email.body1:
Jeremy, saw Placer.ai's civic side picking up fast, with cities and counties leaning on your location data for grants and planning into 2026.

When a new vertical takes off, the list of in-market agencies usually outpaces what the team can cover before budgets cycle. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for your civic motion off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jeremy, quick follow-up on the civic side at Placer.

Government buying cycles are slow and seasonal, so most teams don't know how many meetings they need now to hit the number when budgets actually open. The gap shows up late, and a missed cycle is hard to recover.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your civic team needs this quarter, plus where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jeremy, last bit of proof for the civic team.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your civic reply rate likely compares to peers selling into government. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jeremy, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling civic pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Standing up a government motion keeps a team heads-down for a while.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a civic sales motion? I'll tailor it to your team either way.
